laws.t: Minimum Wages and Conditions of Employment (Domestic Workers) Order, 2011
laws.tp: Minimum wage, hours, rest and leave for domestic workers.
laws.s2: Upah minimum, jam kerja, istirahat, dan cuti bagi pekerja rumah tangga.

coded.vl: General labor law applies, or a dedicated statute grants its core rights
coded.n: Employment law with a sectoral order for domestic workers.
coded.src: Employment Code Act 2019; Domestic Workers Order 2011

coded.fn: Written contract in a language understood
coded.vl: Written contract required, no language rule
A separate or lower minimum, or one set only by policy
coded.n: Sectoral minimum wage for domestic workers.

coded.vl: At least monthly payment, documented, with limits on deductions or in-kind pay
Normal hours limited as for other workers
At least 24 consecutive hours, not replaceable by pay at the employer's request
Equal to or longer than for other workers

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: General rule only, not specific to domestic workers or without a penalty
Accommodation standards only; living in may be required
Change allowed only in listed cases or after conditions are met
coded.n: Work permits tied to the employer.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
coded.n: Labour office and Industrial Relations Court.

coded.vl: Partial: medical care, injury cover or employer insurance only

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence
coded.vl: General criminal or civil law only
May form and join trade unions

dec.ct: African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights
dec.pe: Zambia rounded up 517 people from West Africa, held them in a camp and flew them out without letting them go to court. The African Commission said this broke the African Charter.
dec.pi: Zambia menangkap 517 orang dari Afrika Barat, menahan mereka di kamp, dan menerbangkan mereka keluar tanpa kesempatan ke pengadilan. Komisi Afrika menyatakan ini melanggar Piagam Afrika.

dec.ct: African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights
dec.pe: Zambia deported two opposition figures who had lived there for decades, calling them prohibited immigrants. The African Commission said they had a right to be heard first.
dec.pi: Zambia mendeportasi dua tokoh oposisi yang sudah tinggal puluhan tahun di sana dengan menyebut mereka imigran terlarang. Komisi Afrika menyatakan mereka berhak didengar dulu.
